# Security help

Answers security questions in Slack from your skills and takes a first
look when someone pastes a GitHub pull request.

```text
npx @grok/agent-sdk init ./security-help --template security-help
```

`init` asks which repos it may read. Skip the prompt with
`--var repos=owner/repo`.

## Run

```text
agent-sdk login
agent-sdk slack create --name "Security Help" --channel-posts
```

The Slack app uses `SECURITY_HELP_SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` and
`SECURITY_HELP_SLACK_APP_TOKEN`. `agent-sdk slack create` writes both values
to `.env.local`.

To watch channel posts, add channel names or IDs to `watch` in
`bot/channels/slack.ts`, then invite the app to each channel. An empty
`watch` keeps channel-post dispatch off. Mentions and DMs work without
this configuration.

```bash
agent-sdk dev
```

Slack is a dedicated bot (`@Security Help`). Mentions, DMs, and channel
watch go through that app. GitHub reads use your Cursor GitHub connection
for the repos in `bot/lib/repos.ts`. Paste a PR URL in Slack, or replay
one in the playground.

## Edit

- `bot/lib/repos.ts`: repos it may read
- `bot/channels/slack.ts`: channel ids to watch (`watch`)
- `bot/skills/faq.md`: answers for your company
- `bot/skills/`: how to look at a PR, a leak, or an access ask
- `bot/instructions.md`: routing

`agent-sdk eval` runs three smoke turns and writes nothing to Slack or GitHub.
